RECREATIONAL.gov_quote: North Dakota's cannabis program is medical-only. State law has no protections for marijuana or marijuana products not purchased from an in-state registered dispensary.
RECREATIONAL.validation_notes: Live audit on 2026-09-09 found gov_section verbatim on https://www.hhs.nd.gov/mm/patients.
RECREATIONAL.question: Is it legal for adults to possess cannabis in the state of North Dakota?
RECREATIONAL.gov_section: Note: an individual with a North Dakota medical marijuana card is only authorized to purchase and possess medical marijuana from one of the eight registered dispensaries in the state. State law has no protections for individuals in North Dakota with marijuana or marijuana products not purchased from an in-state registered dispensary.

sourceNotes: This pass started from https://www.hhs.nd.gov/mm on 2026-09-08 and stayed on hhs.nd.gov. That is the Department of Health and Human Services Medical Marijuana Program homepage. A browser-headed fetch of /mm and /mm/patients returned 200 with the quote text in the HTML, so fetch is enough and requires_browser is false. The host can still take a long time to assemble pages, so a short audit timeout can make its rows look unread; raise the timeout rather than replacing the citation. The patients page at /mm/patients is the HTML page that answers possession, dispensary purchase, and the ban on marijuana not bought from an in-state registered dispensary. The program homepage itself is a directory of those pages and does not carry the older arrest-or-prosecution excerpt. State Laws and Administrative Rules at /mm/state-laws-and-administrative-rules only links to PDFs and was not cited. The previously stored recreational citation on ndlegis.gov was a PDF, which hard rule 3 does not allow, and it was replaced because this re-research answered that question from the requested host. The registration portal at mmregistration.health.nd.gov is linked from the program homepage as the application system and was not used as a citation.
